Beyond the visible lesion: mycotoxin attenuation and spatial heterogeneity in maize cobs
nodes.venue: Mycotoxin Research
nodes.abstract: Abstract Visible mould is widely used as a practical sorting cue in maize, but it remains unclear whether the visible lesion marks the boundary of mycotoxin contamination within an intact cob. This study examined mycotoxin attenuation, spatial heterogeneity, and co-occurrence in visibly mouldy white maize cobs, using measured distances from the visible mould margin. Cobs with visible mould ( n = 35) were sampled for the study. For each cob, the visible mould margin was coded as 0 mm, and adjacent sections were collected at the 50% and 75% points along the measured distance from the lesion boundary to the distal cob tip, resulting in 98 cob-section observations. Mycotoxins, FUMs (FB1, FB2, FB3), deoxynivalenol (DON), zearalenone (ZEA), nivalenol (NIV) and AF (AFB1) were quantified by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry. Samples with no detectable levels of mycotoxins were replaced with zero, and total FUMs were calculated (FB1 + FB2 + FB3). The visible mould margin accounted for the largest share of the measured toxin burden, accounting for 84.4% of total FUM, 89.4% of DON, 77.8% of ZEA, and 92.2% of NIV. Adjacent sections retained measurable residual mycotoxins, including 15.6% of total FUM, 10.6% of DON, 22.2% of ZEA, and 7.8% of NIV. In full-distance models, DON, ZEA, and NIV declined significantly with distance, whereas total FUM did not show significant monotonic attenuation. The AFB1 was detected in only three cob sections; these detections co-occurred with Fusarium -associated toxins. Co-occurrence analysis showed that adjacent sections frequently remained positive for multiple Fusarium -associated toxin groups, with the FUM + DON + ZEA profile persisting across measured-distance bands. These findings show that visible mould is a useful warning signal but not a reliable toxicological boundary. The results support cob-level rejection or segregation of visibly mouldy cobs before shelling, rather than lesion-level trimming, as a more defensible food-safety control measure.

nodes.name: Breaking GUI Agent Actions: Realistic Adversarial Attacks on Multimodal LLMs
nodes.venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
nodes.abstract: Recent progress in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has enabled GUI agents that interpret interface screenshots and execute natural-language instructions. However, their increasing role in human–computer interaction raises security concerns. Existing work shows that MLLMs are highly sensitive to interface perturbations, yet most attacks assume unrealistic capabilities such as direct access to model-ready inputs. In real deployments, attackers cannot control the screenshot pipeline or the non-differentiable preprocessing operations preceding inference, rendering many prior attacks ineffective. We introduce Realistic Adversarial Attack (RAA) framework that models the complete screenshot-to-prediction pipeline. To address gradient blockage from non-differentiable preprocessing (e.g., resizing and quantization), we develop a dual-branch differentiable preprocessing module that restores gradient flow while remaining faithful to the actual inference path. To improve robustness against query phrasing changes, we further incorporate a task-level semantic variation mechanism that jointly optimizes over paraphrased task variants. Experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B-Instruct and GUI-Owl-7B show that RAA consistently outperforms prior attacks, improving attack success rates by an average of 30% under localized perturbations and a 10.7% under global perturbations, while maintaining strong effectiveness against standard defenses such as resizing, compression, and noise. Ablation studies highlight the roles of perturbation region and semantic diversity. Our framework establishes a practical threat model for GUI agents and offers a foundation for future robustness and security research.

nodes.name: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing, Communications, and Applications
A Physics‐Informed Two‐Stage Retrieval Method for EMIT Remote Sensing Methane Plumes
nodes.venue: Journal of Geophysical Research: Atmospheres
nodes.abstract: Abstract Hyperspectral satellite missions, particularly EMIT, have revolutionized methane point source monitoring. However, current operational retrieval pipelines typically rely on physically‐based matched filters followed by labor‐intensive manual verification to mitigate high false alarm rates caused by complex background interference. This dependence on human intervention restricts the scalability and efficiency required for rapid, automated global monitoring. To address these limitations, this paper proposes Plume‐Net, a novel Physics‐Informed Guided Two‐Stage Retrieval Method. Unlike conventional approaches, Plume‐Net decouples the task into a “global existence classification” stage and a “local pixel‐level regression” stage to maximize reliability without human‐in‐the‐loop. The core innovation lies in the integration of physical priors with deep learning: In the first stage, a Physics‐Informed Spectral Gating (PISG) module explicitly injects methane spectral absorption knowledge into the network, dynamically recalibrating channel weights to suppress background noise. In the second stage, to overcome the difficulties of regressing sparse, long‐tail plume distributions, we propose a Plume‐Focused Sampling Strategy and an Intensity‐Aware Pixel‐Level Weighted Loss function, forcing the network to prioritize rare but critical high‐concentration signals. Evaluated on real‐world EMIT observations, Plume‐Net achieves an ROC‐AUC of 0.961 in detection and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 33.33 ppm·m in quantification. By significantly reducing false positives while maintaining high precision, this method offers a robust, fully automated alternative to current semi‐manual retrieval workflows.

nodes.name: Bridging spatial scales in respiratory viral infection
nodes.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
nodes.abstract: Respiratory viruses spread within the host through a combination of local expansion and occasional long-range dissemination that seeds new infection foci. We present LEAP (Lotka-Euler Airway Pathogen model), an analytically tractable within-host model that captures this two-scale process. The model takes the form of an age-dependent branching process and yields a closed-form expression for the exponential growth rate during early infection. Using empirical data to parameterize the model, we find that productive dissemination requires only a small number of successful long-range seeding events per infected cell, with distinct values for SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A virus. LEAP further predicts that, in these well-adapted viruses, interferon-mediated restriction only weakly affects exponential growth, while remaining decisive for poorly adapted pathogens. More broadly, the model provides a flexible framework for experimentally testable predictions of early infection dynamics.

nodes.name: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
Voice patches in the marmoset auditory cortex revealed by multimodal optical imaging
nodes.venue: Science Advances
nodes.abstract: Species-specific vocalizations (including human voices) are important for the survival and social interactions of both humans and animals. In both humans and nonhuman primates, voice/vocalization–selective regions have been identified on the lateral temporal cortex. Here, we provide evidence of localized and hierarchically organized voice patches in the auditory cortex of the common marmoset, a highly vocal New World primate, using multimodal optical imaging techniques that directly measure activity from the smooth cortical surface in a noise-controlled environment. Both intrinsic imaging and calcium imaging data revealed two discrete voice patches in a region of the auditory cortex. Our results provided precise functional localization of the two voice patches (posterior and anterior) by anchoring their positions to the tonotopic map and core/noncore areas of the auditory cortex. Both patches preferentially respond to marmoset vocalizations, exhibit quantifiable neural selectivity beyond spectral features, and encode call type and caller identity. Distinct response properties reveal functional differentiation between the posterior and anterior voice patches, with latency differences consistent with a hierarchical relationship. These findings provide new evidence for an evolutionarily conserved cortical architecture in primates that supports vocal communication via voice patches, analogous to face processing systems in human and nonhuman primate brains.

nodes.name: Predicting upcoming visual features during eye movements yields scene representations aligned with human visual cortex
nodes.venue: Science Advances
nodes.abstract: Natural scenes are complex arrangements of objects, surfaces, and backgrounds. For the brain’s visual system to effectively operate, it needs to extract not only what objects are present but also their spatial and semantic relations. We hypothesize that such structures may be learned, in a self-supervised fashion, by exploiting temporal regularities of natural active vision: Each fixation reveals a glimpse that is related to the previous one via co-occurrence and saccade-conditioned spatial regularities. We instantiate this idea with glimpse prediction networks (GPNs), recurrent models trained to predict the embedding of the next glimpse along human-like scanpaths. GPNs are shown to successfully extract complex scene information, including object co-occurrences and spatial object arrangements, and integrate information across glimpses. GPN representations align strongly with human fMRI responses in mid- and higher-level visual cortex and match, often outperform, alternative state-of-the-art ANN models, establishing next-glimpse-prediction as a biologically plausible route toward brain-aligned scene representations.

nodes.name: In-memory phononic learning toward cognitive mechanical intelligence
nodes.venue: Science Advances
nodes.abstract: Mechanical intelligence seeks autonomous materials that embody memory, perception, learning, and decision-making within the mechanical domain. A fundamental challenge is to integrate memory with information processing in an efficient, scalable, and interpretable way that supports cognitive learning and decision-making. Here, we introduce in-memory phononic learning, a framework that unifies non-volatile mechanical memory with wave-based perception in a phononic metastructure. Spatial information is stored as structural states that program elastic-wave responses, allowing probing waves to act as queries that retrieve informative features through parallel, physically transparent localization modes. Learning is achieved by offline optimization of input waveforms to selectively combine these features for multitask memory-pattern recognition without hardware redesign, with decisions inferred directly from output-energy responses. We experimentally and numerically demonstrate high-accuracy classification across tasks from geometric shapes to handwritten digits. Overall, this work elevates “materials that compute” toward “cognitive matter” that can interpret, reason, and learn through wave physics, laying a foundation for scalable and robust autonomous material systems.

nodes.name: A localization and quantification method of Fe <sub>3</sub> O <sub>4</sub> magnetic nanoparticles based on MRX and unscented Kalman filter
nodes.venue: Measurement Science and Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) have attracted extensive research attention in the field of nanomedicine owing to their distinctive magnetic properties and relaxation behaviors. Nevertheless, accurate localization and quantitative estimation of MNPs remain challenging under harsh measurement conditions, such as ultra-low particle concentration and low signal-to-noise ratio. To overcome the aforementioned challenges, we develop an MNP point-source localization and quantification approach integrating magnetic relaxometry and the unscented Kalman filter (UKF). By combining the relaxation theoretical model—moment superposition model and point-source forward model into a unified measurement model, this method fully leverages the time-varying evolution information contained in relaxation signals. Moreover, the UKF is further employed to realize the joint state estimation of particle spatial coordinates and mass. Multiple replicate measurements are performed on physical gel phantoms via a custom-built platform for magnetization and relaxation signal acquisition. Experimental results reveal that the proposed method achieves localization precision superior to 1 mm, with mass quantification errors below 30 μ g. Compared with conventional linear reconstruction approaches, this UKF-based method exhibits stronger robustness against residual sinusoidal noise and system nonlinear dynamics, and its superiority is particularly prominent in the detection of trace amounts of particles. A comprehensive technical framework covering signal acquisition, data preprocessing and nonlinear state estimation is established in this work, yielding a systematic scheme for accurate localization and quantification of MNPs. Significant application prospects can be anticipated for the presented approach in magnetic particle imaging, targeted drug delivery monitoring, in vivo tracer detection and other relevant disciplines.

nodes.name: Towards high-performance image-grade LiDAR odometry and mapping
nodes.venue: Fourth International Conference on Remote Sensing, Mapping, and Geographic Information Systems (RSMG 2026)
nodes.abstract: Image-grade LiDARs can provide dense range measurements and high angular resolution, which makes them attractive for vehicle localization and map construction. However, the large number of points and the limited field of view also increase the difficulty of real-time and robust odometry estimation, especially in tunnels, urban roads, and other geometrically degraded scenes. In this paper, we develop a LiDAR-only SLAM framework for image-grade LiDARs. The system is formulated atop a factor graph, where denoised and distortion-free point clouds are projected onto a range image. Ground, planar, and edge features are extracted using a degeneracy-aware feature selection strategy for pose estimation, while line features are further incorporated in structured environments. To improve robustness under the limited FoV, a mixed loop detection strategy combining trajectory and structural information is introduced. Experiments in several realworld scenes show that the proposed system can produce consistent trajectories and maps while maintaining real-time performance.

nodes.name: Fourth International Conference on Remote Sensing, Mapping, and Geographic Information Systems (RSMG 2026)
Text-Prompted Multimodal Object Detection with Structural and Frequency-Decoupled Enhancement for UAV Imagery
nodes.venue: Engineering Research Express
nodes.abstract: Abstract Complex scene perception and dense small object detection in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery frequently encounter severe challenges, including extremely small object scales, strong background interference, and severe occlusion. Conventional vision-only detection frameworks typically perform feature extraction and fusion solely at the pixel level, lacking the synergy between explicit semantic information and fine-grained localization cues. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel multimodal object detection framework driven by text prompts, alongside frequency-domain and structural priors. First, a text semantic prompting mechanism is introduced to transform closed-set detection into a cross-modal feature alignment task, utilizing multimodal semantics to explicitly direct visual representations toward target regions. Second, in the deep encoding stage, an Adaptive Differentiable Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG)-Guided Self-Attention (ADGA) module is designed to inject multi-scale continuous gradient features as structural priors into the self-attention computation. During the feature fusion stage, a Competitive Interactive Dynamic Alignment Fusion (CAF) module is proposed. By explicitly modeling the discrepancies and consistency among feature branches and introducing a competitive allocation mechanism, it achieves a content-driven reorganization of features at the same scale. Finally, in the pre-decoder stage, a Frequency-Decoupled Dual Attention (FDDA) module is introduced. It utilizes differentiable Gaussian soft masks to decouple high-frequency and low-frequency components and applies customized spatial and channel attention, respectively, thereby providing high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) features for the decoder. Extensive experiments on the VisDrone2019 dataset demonstrate that the proposed model achieves an overall Average Precision (AP) of 0.246 and a small object average precision (APs) of 0.171, with only 15.80M parameters and 30.92 GFLOPs. Furthermore, additional experiments on the UAVDT dataset yield an AP of 0.225, an AP50 of 0.357, and an APs of 0.154, further demonstrating the robustness and cross-dataset generalization capability of the proposed framework in diverse UAV scenarios.

nodes.name: TRACE-Loc: Causal Trajectory-Constrained Cross-View Localization for GNSS-Denied UAVs
nodes.venue: Drones
nodes.abstract: UAV-to-satellite visual localization can provide absolute position observations when Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals are denied or lost. Without a reliable initial position, however, cross-view differences and repetitive textures can cause single-frame retrieval to jump to distant but visually similar regions. This paper presents TRACE-Loc, an online trajectory-constrained cross-view retrieval framework for initial localization. A DINOv3 frontend with view-conditioned low-rank adaptation (VC-LoRA) generates current-frame candidates from a global satellite gallery. The online reranker projects recent location hypotheses using heading, elapsed time, and causal visual speed, then recursively selects a motion-consistent path from the union of current retrievals and historical projections. The path recursion without historical projection coincides with a beam-width-limited Viterbi decode over the retrieval candidates, so the method can be read as beam Viterbi plus causal candidate projection. Experiments use a unified gallery of 15,130 UAV-VisLoc satellite tiles and 1215 queries from two regions excluded from both training and parameter selection. Across three independent training runs, TRACE-Loc raises C@1 from 48.67 ± 0.41% to 58.33 ± 2.84%, a paired gain of 9.66 ± 2.69 percentage points; the single representative run used for detailed comparisons increases C@1 from 49.05% to 61.23%, reduces median localization error from 150.92 m to 93.75 m, and raises D < 300 m from 53.66% to 70.62%. The same reranker improves C@1 across six retrieval frontends. In reset-at-every-start cold-start evaluation, TRACE-Loc increases the Kaplan–Meier probability of obtaining a stable fix within 30 s over single-frame retrieval by 2.33, 9.27, and 5.89 percentage points at the 50, 100, and 300 m thresholds (paired block-bootstrap 95% CIs excluding zero at every threshold), while the particle filter attains statistically indistinguishable early-fix probabilities and recovers faster over longer observation periods; the reported gains therefore concern acquisition from an empty state relative to single-frame retrieval, not an advantage over the particle filter. These results show that candidate-level trajectory constraints improve framewise localization in a large gallery with millisecond-level reranking overhead and increase the probability of an early stable fix.

nodes.name: Spatial distribution and prediction of local wind-driven rain intensity on building façades: Reduced-scale experiments and model validation
nodes.venue: Indoor and Built Environment
nodes.abstract: Wind-driven rain (WDR) creates highly nonuniform moisture loads on building façades, challenging waterproofing design and durability assessment. Existing WDR studies have emphasized overall exposure and spatial patterns, with limited attention to predicting local exposure across varying wind and rain conditions. This study conducted controlled indoor experiments on a reduced-scale façade model to characterize local WDR exposure. Analysis of 684 windward façade data points showed consistently high catch ratios in the upper and corner regions. Wind speed dominated variation in catch ratio, wind direction redistributed WDR between façades, and rainfall intensity mainly controlled water input. Within the experimental design, wind speed, wind direction, and rainfall intensity explained 74.30%, 20.13%, and 1.44% of the variance in mean catch ratio, respectively. A local WDR intensity model was developed by incorporating a position correction coefficient into an established semiempirical relationship. Validation yielded an RMSE of 0.371 mm/h, an MAE of 0.286 mm/h, and a relative bias of +1.06%. By extending WDR intensity prediction from façade-averaged to location-specific values, the model captures local exposure peaks and provides spatially resolved rain inputs for zoned waterproofing and hygrothermal simulations. It may also support targeted protection of traditional buildings exposed to long-term WDR.

nodes.name: Short-form travel video characteristics and travel intention: a meta-analytic structural equation modeling study of the indirect role of destination image
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Communication
nodes.abstract: Introduction Short-form video is increasingly important in destination communication, but evidence on its associations with travel intention and the role of destination image remains fragmented. Methods Following a preregistered protocol and a transparently reported postregistration journal-only amendment, we synthesized nine independent samples ( N = 3,200) reporting correlations among short-form travel video characteristics, destination image, and travel intention. Random-effects two-stage meta-analytic structural equation modeling pooled study-level correlation matrices. Results Video characteristics correlated positively with destination image ( r = 0.514) and travel intention ( r = 0.492), while destination image correlated with travel intention ( r = 0.541). Structural paths were a = 0.514, b = 0.391, and c′ = 0.291. The indirect association was ab = 0.201, 95% CI [0.133, 0.290]. Expanded exposure-boundary, reconstructed-proxy exclusion, and leave-one-out analyses yielded the same substantive pattern. Discussion The findings are consistent with partial statistical mediation but not causal mediation. Interpretation remains constrained by cross-sectional self-report evidence, inadequate confounder control, substantial heterogeneity, geographic concentration, incomplete retrieval, and incomplete coverage of planned sources. Systematic Review Registration https://osf.io/5vhet/ , identifier 5vhet.

nodes.name: Satellite-based Assessment of Continuous and Episodic Flaring Regimes across Major Oil and Gas-producing Basins
nodes.abstract: Gas flaring wastes valuable natural gas while emitting large amounts of harmful air pollutants; however, existing flare inventories rarely distinguish the operational behavior across various basins and fuel types, namely oil- and gas-associated flaring.This limits their value for targeted mitigation efforts. Here, we present a satellite-based classification framework for characterizing flaring behavior by combining coarse resolution Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) Nightfire (VNF) products with high-spatial resolution Sentinel-2 and Landsat~8/9 imagery. The framework quantifies temporal persistence and identifies operational interruptions from daily VIIRS thermal records, while using Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8/9 imagery to characterize flare site conditions at higher spatial resolution. It then assigns fuel type as oil or gas, yielding four operational categories: continuous oil/gas and episodic oil/gas. Applied to Algeria, Iran, Mexico, Nigeria, Saudi Arabia, and Turkmenistan, the framework identified 1,910 confirmed flare sites, approximately 1.8 times the number detected by VIIRS alone. Our analysis shows that continuous oil flares are the largest category, with 728 sites representing 56% of the classified inventory. Iran has the largest number of continuous oil flares (262) and a more geographically concentrated pattern. Gas flares account for 25% of the classified sites and form the majority of the classified flares in Turkmenistan. These sites were then linked to the gas pipeline infrastructure and compared with multi-scale methane observations. The analysis shows that Iran and Algeria contain the largest flare volumes near gas pipelines, whereas Mexico has a more spatially concentrated recovery opportunity close to existing infrastructure. Oil flares, particularly continuous oil flares, are more frequently co-located with methane plumes in Algeria and Iran than in other countries. Although Saudi Arabia has a high flare count, it has no matched methane plumes. These results reveal systematic differences in the proximity of the infrastructure and the detectability of methane, providing a transferable basis for mitigation prioritization and source attribution.

nodes.name: STCA-Net: A Spatiotemporal Cross-Attention Network with Multi-Scale Depthwise Separable Convolutions for Epileptic EEG Seizure Classification
nodes.abstract: Abstract Automated epileptic seizure classification from electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings can assist the analysis of large volumes of neurological data and reduce the burden associated with manual interpretation. However, distinguishing EEG patterns across different seizure-related and non-seizure classes remains challenging because relevant information occurs at multiple temporal scales and may involve both local and long-range dependencies. To address these challenges, we propose STCA-Net, a compact spatiotemporal neural architecture that combines multi-scale convolutional feature extraction with cross-attention-based feature fusion. The network consists of four principal components: a Depthwise Separable Convolutional Attention (DSCA) module with multiple kernel sizes for extracting local temporal patterns, a Temporal Pyramid Pooling (TPP) module for multi-scale contextual aggregation, a Compact Temporal Encoder (CTE) for modelling long-range temporal dependencies with reduced computational cost, and a Bidirectional Cross-Attention Fusion (CAF) module for exchanging information between spatial and temporal representations. Experiments are conducted on the University of Bonn EEG dataset using stratified cross-validation for binary, three-class, and five-class classification tasks. STCA-Net achieves an accuracy of 97.58% ± 0.77% for binary classification, 93.09% ± 1.31% for three-class classification, and 75.64% ± 1.27% for five-class classification, with a corresponding five-class F1-score of 75.50% ± 1.26%. In the five-class setting, the proposed method improves accuracy and F1-score over the MASF baseline by 3.14 and 2.88 percentage points, respectively. Ablation experiments further demonstrate the contribution of bidirectional cross-attention compared with direct feature concatenation. With approximately 46,885 trainable parameters, STCA-Net provides a compact architecture for EEG classification while maintaining competitive predictive performance.

nodes.name: STB-Track: HMA-Net for Precise Target Localization and Tracking in Complex Scenarios
nodes.venue: Engineering Research Express
nodes.abstract: Abstract Target tracking becomes highly challenging in complex scenarios that include background distractors similar to the target, partial occlusion of the target, or significant scale variations. Most current trackers construct tracking templates by focusing on the target itself. However, under conditions such as occlusion or the presence of background distractors similar to the target, these methods often fail to fully leverage the spatial relationships between adjacent image patches. The extracted features lack sufficient discriminative power for similar objects, leading to a loss of spatial information about the target and a tendency to fall into local optima, which makes predicting the target state difficult. To address these limitations, this study aims to enhance the feature extraction network's capability to capture information from adjacent image patches and integrate local and global features to improve the discriminative ability for similar objects. This paper constructs a joint optimization framework based on Swin Transformer, which employs a shifted window strategy to focus on the interactions between adjacent image patches in each frame. To overcome the insufficient discriminative power of features extracted by existing methods for similar objects, we propose a feature fusion network (HMA-Net) that uses a multi-scale attention mechanism based on the traditional Transformer. In the first stage, spatial-channel reconstruction convolution is combined with a self-attention mechanism to capture contextual information at different scales. In the second stage, a dual-layer routing attention mechanism is used to enhance the output of the cross-attention mechanism regarding the correlations between image regions, and similarity is computed within local regions. Additionally, we integrate classification and regression tasks through an enhanced prediction head for the loss function. Extensive experiments were conducted on large public datasets such as LaSOT, GOT-10k, and TrackingNet. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method maintains high localization accuracy and tracking stability under various complex environmental conditions, achieving competitive performance on most benchmark datasets.

nodes.name: Restorative streetscapes in high-density urban tourism: environmental archetypes, visual attention, and psychophysiological responses
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Public Health
nodes.abstract: In high-density tourist districts, visitors are continuously exposed to the visual environments of surrounding streets, forecourts, and small public spaces before reaching an attraction, and these transitional spaces may influence short-term restorative states. Existing research has typically examined urban-scale streetscape characteristics and human responses under experimental conditions separately, with limited provision of a reproducible procedure for selecting experimental stimuli from large environmental samples. Taking the high-density urban core around Hong Kong’s Victoria Harbour as a case study, this study identified 66 tourism-related sites and acquired four fixed-direction streetscape images for each site, yielding 264 images in total. A 66 × 11 objective environmental matrix was constructed from five GIS-based environmental indicators and six streetscape-image proxy indicators. Principal component analysis (PCA) summarized the dominant environmental gradients, and k = 6 K-means was retained as a pragmatic six-group sampling solution aligned with the pre-specified six-scene experimental capacity rather than as a uniquely optimal or stable urban typology. Forty-six of 48 registered adults contributed 108 focal-scene exposures. After BH-FDR correction, significant differences among the six scenes were observed in perceived restorativeness, the proportion of fixations on natural areas of interest (AOIs), gaze entropy, changes in EEG alpha-minus-theta, mean EDA skin conductance level (SCL), and HRV RMSSD, whereas sustained-attention accuracy showed no significant scene effect. Oil Street Art Space exhibited the highest perceived restorativeness (5.69/7), the highest proportion of fixations on natural AOIs (51.4%), and the largest increases in EEG (+2.68) and HRV RMSSD (+11.37 ms), while Western Market showed the lowest restorativeness (4.17/7), the lowest natural-AOI fixation share (31.2%), and the smallest EEG increase (+1.93). Sensitivity analyses showed no evidence of scene-by-order interaction for perceived restorativeness, natural-AOI fixation, gaze entropy, or SART accuracy, but EEG, EDA, and HRV were more order-sensitive; the principal subjective, attentional, EEG, and HRV contrasts remained evident when analysis was restricted to each participant’s earliest focal-scene exposure. These findings therefore support scene-configuration contrasts under short-term static visual exposure. Building on the environmental structure of the 66 sites and the multimodal responses to the six experimental scenes, the study further proposes an archetype-calibrated framework for mapping restorative potential in high-density tourist streetscapes, providing a spatial basis for identifying restorative opportunity nodes and priority intervention areas.

nodes.name: Regional-Scale Object Feature Recognition in High-Resolution Remote Sensing Images Based on YOLOv8
nodes.venue: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
nodes.abstract: Accurate object detection in regional-scale remote sensing imagery is challenged by significant scale variation, dense small targets, and complex background interference. While mainstream detection frameworks have achieved competitive results, their performance often declines when directly applied to high-resolution aerial scenes. To address this issue, this paper presents an enhanced YOLOv8-based detection framework and conducts a systematic comparative evaluation against representative state-of-the-art methods. A lightweight attention-guided multi-scale feature refinement module is introduced to strengthen small object representation, and an optimized feature aggregation strategy is adopted to improve localization precision without increasing computational complexity. Experiments are performed on two widely used remote sensing datasets, NWPU VHR-10 and DIOR. The proposed method achieves consistent performance improvements over competitive mainstream detectors, with approximately 1.98% gain in mAP while preserving real-time efficiency. Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the proposed refinement mechanism. The results demonstrate that the improved YOLOv8 framework provides a robust and efficient solution for regional-scale remote sensing object detection.

nodes.name: International Journal of Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence
Recognition and parametric modeling of existing tunnel facilities using mobile laser scanning and YOLOv8
nodes.venue: Fourth International Conference on Remote Sensing, Mapping, and Geographic Information Systems (RSMG 2026)
nodes.abstract: The digital management of existing metro tunnels requires accurate facility information and 3D models. However, design drawings and manually maintained inventories often fail to reflect the current state of tunnel facilities after long-term operation and equipment replacement. This study proposes a workflow that integrates mobile laser scanning, YOLOv8 recognition, and Revit Dynamo modeling for tunnel facility recognition and parametric model generation. Intensity orthoimages are generated from MLS point clouds based on the actual tunnel contour, and local regions are extracted to identify rail fasteners, catenary support brackets, lighting equipment, balises, and evacuation signs. The detected targets are converted into modeling parameters, including facility category, tunnel mileage, circumferential position, and detection confidence. These parameters are imported into Dynamo to automatically place corresponding Revit components. Experiments show that the proposed workflow can identify key tunnel facilities and generate BIM elements in batches. The method provides practical data support for facility inventory, maintenance management, and digital updating of existing tunnels.

nodes.name: RadarSEDiff-T: Radar Structured-Encoding Diffusion with Transformer Guidance for Radar Sensing Enhancement
nodes.abstract: Abstract Leveraging the unique advantages of all-weather anti-interference capability and deep hardware reuse with 6G communication systems, millimeter-wave radar has emerged as the most promising native perception carrier for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) scenarios.However, its inherent limitations of sparse point cloud distribution and low angular resolution prevent it from achieving LiDAR-level perception accuracy, which severely hinders its deployment in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) autonomous navigation applications.To address this issue, we propose RadarSEDiff-T, an optimized latent diffusion model designed to reconstruct dense LiDAR-level point clouds from a single millimeter-wave radar frame. Specifically, we first design a point-cloud-like structure tailored to the unique properties of radar bird's-eye view (BEV) maps, and train a dedicated radar encoder RSE independently. We further replace the conventional U-Net architecture with stacked Transformer blocks, enabling multi-dimensional millimeter-wave radar features to guide the entire diffusion generation process through global modeling and attention modules.Moreover, we integrate a consistency model to accelerate the inference of the diffusion model, ensuring that the proposed method can be effectively deployed on resource-constrained UAV platforms. We evaluate our approach on the public RadarHD dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on the millimeter-wave radar super-resolution task, and explicitly verifies the significant speed advantage of our enhanced diffusion framework.

nodes.name: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
nodes.venue: Nature Methods
nodes.abstract: Abstract Deep visual proteomics (DVP) is an emerging approach for cell-type-specific and spatially resolved proteomics. However, its broad adoption has been constrained by the lack of an open-source end-to-end workflow within a community-driven ecosystem. Here we introduce openDVP, an experimental and computational framework for accessible and scalable DVP. OpenDVP combines open-source image analysis tools (MCMICRO, QuPath and napari) with scverse formats (AnnData and SpatialData) for multiomics integration. It provides two workflows: a fast-track pipeline requiring no image analysis expertise, and an artificial intelligence-powered pipeline incorporating state-of-the-art methods for image preprocessing, segmentation and spatial analysis. We apply openDVP across three archival tissue studies (human placenta, early stage lung cancer and locally relapsed breast cancer), integrating spatial single-cell phenotypes with exploratory proteomic measurements. Finally, we introduce deep proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods as a scalable approach for spatial discovery proteomics.

nodes.name: Multisource satellite remote sensing for eco-environmental monitoring of power grids: progress and frontier trends
nodes.venue: Fourth International Conference on Remote Sensing, Mapping, and Geographic Information Systems (RSMG 2026)
nodes.abstract: The rapid expansion of power grids has induced complex eco-environmental impacts along transmission corridors. Multisource satellite remote sensing has emerged as an indispensable tool for monitoring these disturbances. This review systematically examines the applications of optical, SAR, thermal infrared, and LiDAR technologies in the life-cycle environmental monitoring of power transmission projects. We outline a robust indicator system encompassing vegetation structural indices, soil erosion models, and surface deformation metrics, while evaluating state-of-the-art parameter retrieval algorithms. Methodological advances—spanning from conventional techniques to deep learning foundation models and multi-source data fusion—are discussed alongside key applications such as soil conservation, vegetation-line conflict detection, and geological hazard assessment. Despite current progress, critical challenges remain regarding spatiotemporal data discontinuity, limited model transferability, InSAR constraints, and the lack of standard validation frameworks. To address these, future directions emphasize dedicated power-sector satellite constellations, edge-cloud collaborative computing, explainable AI, and rigorous uncertainty quantification. Ultimately, this review provides a technical roadmap for the precise monitoring and ecological governance of power grid infrastructure. To clarify its scope, this article is positioned as a framework-based systematic review with a reproducible literature screening protocol, organized around a data sources-monitoring indicators-retrieval and fusion methods-application scenarios-technical challenges-future trends analytical chain.

nodes.name: Multisource remote sensing assessment of OpenStreetMap coastline quality in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area
nodes.venue: Fourth International Conference on Remote Sensing, Mapping, and Geographic Information Systems (RSMG 2026)
nodes.abstract: The reliability of volunteered geographic information (VGI) for scientific applications depends on systematic quality evaluation. This study develops a five-dimensional framework to assess OpenStreetMap (OSM) coastline quality in the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), using GlobeLand30 (GCL_FCS30, 2010/2015/2020), Sentinel- 2 Level-2A imagery, and county-level administrative boundaries. Five quality dimensions are evaluated across 2,705 OSM coastline segments: (1) positional accuracy via minimum-distance spatial sampling (1,987 points, 1 per km of OSM coastline); (2) classification accuracy via semantic cross-walk with GCL land cover; (3) temporal dynamics via multi-epoch GCL change detection; (4) spatial completeness at district level; and (5) conditional NDWI-based remote sensing cross-check (single-tidal-realisation). Against GCL2020, OSM coastlines exhibit a median positional offset of 1,090 m (20 m match rate: 15.8%). Artificial coastlines (Class 0) achieve 98.3% user’s accuracy, while natural coastlines (Class 4) reach only 13.5%. GCL records a 181.6% expansion of artificial coastlines (2010–2020), reflecting rapid land reclamation. OSM coverage is spatially biased toward Hong Kong, with only 29.2% of all districts holding any data. Sentinel-2 NDWI cross-check conditionally confirms Class 0 reliability (median offset: 229 m; MR50m: 40.9%), subject to tidal-stage limitations. These results provide a quantitative basis for selective use of OSM coastline data in GBA coastal research.

nodes.name: Multimodal Detection for Underwater Cultural Heritage: A Physics-Guided Color-Bias-Aware Network and Dataset
nodes.abstract: Abstract Reliable object detection is essential for underwater cultural heritage research, yet its development remains limited by the scarcity of domain-specific annotations, underwater color distortion, and attenuated object boundaries. To address these challenges, we construct the Wrecks, Ruins, and Fragmentary heritage (WRF) dataset, comprising 4,732 RGB images collected from multiple underwater archaeological sites, corresponding estimated depth maps, 17,059 annotated instances, and 21 categories of artifacts and ship components. We further develop UCH-Net, a dual-stream RGB-depth detector that integrates appearance and geometric cues through physics-guided color-bias-aware fusion, multi-scale feature aggregation, and decoupled localization. On the WRF, UCH-Net achieves an mAP of 77.5% and an mAP75 of 88.0%, surpassing the representative Deformable-DETR baseline by 12.8 and 14.9 percentage points, respectively, while exceeding the strongest competing results by 1.2% in mAP75 and 1.5% in recall. UCH-Net further achieves an mAP of 66.0% on RUOD. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed dataset and detector for automated screening and object localization in underwater archaeological imagery.

nodes.name: MSF-SG-DeepLabV3+ network for land-cover recognition in high-resolution remote sensing images
nodes.venue: Fourth International Conference on Remote Sensing, Mapping, and Geographic Information Systems (RSMG 2026)
nodes.abstract: To address pronounced target-scale variation, ambiguous inter-class boundaries, and the fragmentation of elongated objects such as roads in land-cover classification using high-resolution remote sensing imagery, this paper proposes a Multi-Scale Fusion Decoder with Semantic Skip Gate (MSF-SG) decoder based on DeepLabV3+. During decoding, a Semantic Skip Gate modulates encoder skip connections at the pixel level according to the current semantic confidence, suppressing redundant textures in high-confidence regions while retaining more structural details in low-confidence and boundary regions. In addition, skip-feature fusion is organized at two scales, H/8 and H/4, to improve the utilization of mid-level structural information and shallow details. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves mIoU scores of 50.38% and 83.13% on the LoveDA and ISPRS Potsdam datasets, respectively. It effectively improves land-cover classification accuracy and shows improved performance in boundary regions and complex land-cover transitions.

nodes.name: Intelligent Academic Search and Research Gap Discovery: A Review of Citation Networks, Knowledge Graphs and Semantic Retrieval
nodes.venue: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management
nodes.abstract: Prepared as a literature-based review related to the development of an Academic Research Intelligence System (ARIS). Scholarly output is growing exponentially. A scientist today cannot easily find, follow and predict what is relevant. I will review two topics: academic intelligence search and search system recommendations, research gap or future direction detection. Five new papers published between 2024-2025 will be discussed: the use of citation networks for paper recommendations, classification of potential future work using a knowledge graph, search system structure for broad academic searches, systems recommending the right authors for a researcher, and a new paper embedding citation- and searching based relationships between papers. Citing works helps map ideas between papers, yet standalone citations sometimes miss meaning. Besides connections, added details like semantic structure and user feedback might boost searching and suggesting related papers. Though useful on their own, references can carry inconsistencies - their presence doesn't always reflect how findings relate. To spot where studies should go next, clear frameworks matter more than scattered clues. A logical sequence begins with finding relevant papers, moves through how they link, then points toward unfinished questions worth exploring. The review provides a research foundation for ARIS without treating ARIS itself as an already validated research system. Keywords Academic search; research paper recommendation; Scitation networks; knowledge graphs; research gaps; semantic retrieval; scholarly information systems.

nodes.name: International Scientific Journal of Engineering and Management
Growth-Point Detection and 3D–2D Two-Stage Localization of Cucurbit Rootstock Seedlings Using YOLO11-Pose-LGA
nodes.venue: Agriculture
nodes.abstract: In automated grafting of cucurbits, variation in growth-point position and morphology of cucurbit rootstock seedlings, together with position deviation caused by picking and grasping, can limit the millimeter-level accuracy required for growth-point cutting. This study proposed a 3D and 2D two-stage visual localization method based on the lightweight YOLO11-Pose-LGA model. In the first stage, RGB-D depth information was used to construct a 3D point set and estimate the 3D position and grasp pose of rootstock seedlings in random poses, thereby guiding adaptive robotic picking. In the second stage, side-view 2D vision was used to fit the V-shaped inner edges of the cotyledons after grasping, relocalize the growth point, and compensate for post-grasp position deviation before cutting. The YOLO11-Pose-LGA model achieved a Pose mAP@0.5:0.95 of 0.916. In physical system tests involving 400 rootstock seedlings, 378 seedlings were successfully picked, corresponding to a 3D vision-guided picking success rate of 94.5% (378/400). The second-stage 2D growth-point relocalization for the 378 successfully picked seedlings produced a vertical MAE of 0.39 mm and a combined MAE of 0.63 mm. After growth-point relocalization and Z-axis height compensation, 342 of the 378 successfully picked seedlings met the cutting qualification criteria, corresponding to a conditional qualified cutting rate of 90.5% (342/378) and an end-to-end successful picking-and-cutting rate of 85.5% (342/400). These results indicate that, under the tested experimental conditions, the proposed 3D global guidance and 2D local compensation framework can support spatial picking guidance for rootstock seedlings in random poses and post-grasp pre-cut growth-point localization for automated grafting operations.

nodes.name: Geospatial approaches to mapping invasive alien plants: the neglected role of soil in remote sensing and GIS-based distribution models
nodes.venue: Frontiers in Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: Introduction Invasive alien plants (IAPs) pose significant ecological and socio‐economic threats by disrupting native biodiversity, ecosystem functioning, and land productivity, underscoring the need for robust spatial tools to guide management interventions. Using a systematic literature review approach guided by the PRISMA framework, this study examines geospatial techniques for modelling Invasive Alien Plant (IAP) distributions, focusing on how climatic, land use/land cover (LULC), and soil variables are integrated to explain habitat suitability. Methods Across reviewed studies, remote sensing and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) emerged as central tools for multi‐scale monitoring and predictor integration. Medium‐resolution satellite imagery (Sentinel‐2, Landsat) commonly supported regional assessments of vegetation change and land-use dynamics, while very‐high‐resolution imagery enabled finer species‐ and structure-level discrimination, though at greater cost. These data streams were increasingly coupled with machine learning and statistical approaches to improve classification accuracy, though performance remained dependent on input data quality and adequate representation of key environmental drivers. Results A notable methodological imbalance emerged in predictor selection. Among the 24 studies included in the soil‐variable integration analysis, 71% (n = 17) excluded soil variables, relying instead on spectral, thermal, and structural proxies, land surface temperature, and canopy characteristics. Only 29% (n = 7) incorporated measured edaphic variables, such as soil pH, texture, and soil classification, which typically require field integration if observations, soil survey data, and digital soil maps within GIS-based frameworks. Discussion This omission stemmed largely from remote sensing’s inability to directly observe below‐ground properties and the logistical challenges of acquiring spatially explicit soil data. The review suggests that the limited integration of soil variables may constrain the ecological realism of geospatial invasion models, particularly in environmentally heterogeneous landscapes. Greater integration of soil, climate and LULC frameworks has the potential to improve ecological realism and predictive capability and warrant further investigation, particularly in under‐studied regions such as Sub-Saharan Africa.

nodes.name: From direct emission factors to inverse and indirect impact factors of road traffic: influence of emerging and unregulated pollutants
nodes.venue: Atmospheric chemistry and physics
nodes.abstract: Abstract. Even though emissions regulations have successfully reduced concentrations of some road traffic-originated air pollutants, road traffic is still an important source of many unregulated emerging pollutants such as semi-volatile ultrafine particles, non-exhaust emissions and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in urban areas. In addition, road traffic can have season- and location-dependent inverse and indirect effects on the urban aerosol which are not well understood. In our study, we investigate wintertime vehicle fleet emission factors (EF) of road traffic in a street canyon environment in central Helsinki, Finland, by using CO2 as a tracer for fuel consumption. We report EFs for particle number and size distribution, black carbon, PM10, PM2.5, NOx, NO2, NO, CO as well as for organic and inorganic chemical components of particulate matter, and VOCs, including aromatic hydrocarbons, alkanes, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons. The obtained fleet EFs of PM and NOx were considerably higher than required for new vehicles in Europe since 2014, showing the major role of older vehicles and heavy-duty traffic on the urban aerosol. In addition to direct EFs, we show that CO2-based EF determination enables detection of inverse and indirect effects of road traffic. For example, road traffic had an inverse effect, i.e., negative EF, on O3 and small ion (< 2 nm) concentrations. Also, we found that road traffic contributes to compounds that are not necessarily considered to be traffic-derived such as terpenoid VOCs. We introduce a term impact factor (IF) to describe the found inverse and indirect effects of road traffic.

nodes.name: From Model Proliferation to Deployment Intelligence: A Risk-Traceable System-Aware Model Selection Framework
nodes.venue: Applied Sciences
nodes.abstract: The rapid growth of machine-learning architectures has shifted an important engineering challenge from model development to selecting the most suitable trained candidate for a specific deployment context. This study proposes the System-Aware Model Selection (SMS) Framework, implemented through the Deployment-Aware Model Selection Algorithm (DAMSA), as a three-layer post-training decision architecture integrating risk-to-criterion mapping, candidate control, reference ranking, and robustness analysis. Across five engineering scenarios, DAMSA-SMS was compared with benchmark-oriented and conventional decision procedures under common candidate evidence and priority assumptions. Conventional multi-criteria procedures generally agreed on the nominal reference winner, but DAMSA-SMS revealed different levels of decision robustness. YOLOv7 was selected for traffic monitoring and pharmaceutical inspection with first-rank acceptabilities of 92.8% and 91.2%, respectively. In defense surveillance, YOLOv8s was preferred to the highest-mAP YOLOv11s because its Precision was 18.9 percentage points higher. YOLOv8s was Pareto-unique and preference-stable in microplastics detection. In CCPP monitoring, Random Forest was preferred under the Testing-Generalization profile, with the decision switching below a 12.99% Generalization Stability weight. Removing F1-score did not change any vision recommendation. These results show that nominal ranking agreement does not necessarily imply deployment robustness.

nodes.name: Evolution of non-stationary quasi-periodic pulsations in solar flares with Aditya-L1/HEL1OS and GOES
nodes.venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences
nodes.abstract: Abstract In the present work, we use a phase-resolved methodology for the detection and characterization of non-stationary quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs) in the hard X-ray light curves observed from the High Energy L1-Orbiting X-ray Spectrometer instrument on board the Aditya-L1 mission, complemented by cross-examination using soft X-ray observations from Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellites. Our approach combines variational mode decomposition with Hilbert–Huang analysis and wavelet transforms to sharpen transient QPP signatures, extract narrowband amplitude–frequency modulated modes and track instantaneous period drift across various phases of the flares. By applying these tools to pre-flare, impulsive and decay phases and associated intervals, we identify the timing, duration and evolution of statistically significant oscillations and assess their relation to thermal and non-thermal flare components. Finally, we extend the method to the catalogue of non-stationary QPP flares reported by Mehta et al. (Mehta et al. 2023 Mon. Not. R. Astron. Soc. 523, 3689–3698. (doi:10.1093/mnras/stad1619)), where we identify statistically significant QPPs in both impulsive and decay phases for 74 out of 98 flares. Among these, 56.8% exhibit small period drifts, while 43.2% show larger deviations. Positive period drift dominates (73%), indicating a systematic increase in characteristic timescales as flares evolve. A phase–period–duration analysis reveals distinct regimes of non-stationarity, including overlapping multi-mode oscillations, intermittent same-period episodes and strongly evolving multi-modal behaviour. This article is part of the theme issue ‘Transferable mechanisms in the oscillatory processes of solar and stellar flares'.

nodes.name: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Sciences
Ecological restoration monitoring system for mining areas using image recognition technology
nodes.venue: Fourth International Conference on Remote Sensing, Mapping, and Geographic Information Systems (RSMG 2026)
nodes.abstract: Open-pit mining causes severe ecological damage requiring efficient monitoring. To overcome the high cost and poor scalability of traditional field surveys, this paper presents an image recognition-based restoration detection system using deep learning and remote sensing. The system integrates three modules: Bare Rock Index (BRI), an improved U-Net for semantic segmentation, and LandTrendr for temporal change detection, enabling automatic assessment from uploaded satellite or UAV images. Built on a front-end/back-end separated architecture (Vue.js front-end, Flask back-end), the system supports image upload, visualization, and data management. Experiments on Pingshuo coal mine and Dexing copper mine datasets show overall accuracy >85%, bare rock recognition accuracy of 90%, and comprehensive restoration accuracy of 86.5%. This system provides a low-cost, scalable tool for mine environmental management and reclamation assessment.

nodes.name: EU forest carbon sink decline as seen by Earth observation and national inventories
nodes.abstract: Abstract. The declining European forest carbon uptake in recent years is challenging the capacity of European forests to remain carbon sinks, while the European Union’s climate policy relies on this large natural carbon sink to meet its climate targets. The decreased forest carbon sink is thought to be caused by a combination of increased harvest, severe droughts, bark beetle infestations, tree mortality, and slow-down in tree growth causing reduced CO2 uptake. Yet several knowledge gaps remain, importantly a lack of a reconciliation and country-scale quantitative comparison of carbon losses from recent forest disturbances. In the past years, several estimates of forest C fluxes and losses over Europe based on remote sensing have been developed, complementing national greenhouse gas inventory (NGHGI) information. However, an in-depth intercomparison between these various approaches is needed to derive common best estimates of recent C losses, as well as define mutual benefits and individual weaknesses of the different data streams. Here we investigate the recent changes in the European forest carbon sink by combining new high-resolution Earth Observation (EO)-based estimates of forest aboveground biomass carbon (AGC), forest disturbance and recovery, EO-based bookkeeping models, atmospheric CO2 inversions, and NGHGI approaches. We find that all datasets agree on a reduction of forest C uptake in 2020–2023 by 17–27 % compared to the average of 1990–2019 (-135 to -233 TgC/yr), with a remaining forest C sink in 2020–2023 in the range of -100 to -193 TgC/yr. Central and boreal European forest C sink losses contribute most substantially to the observed reduction of the net forest C sink over Europe. This increase in C losses is more strongly driven by effects of natural disturbance than increased harvest, where natural disturbance C losses increased 2.6-fold in central and 1.4-fold in boreal Europe in 2020–23 compared to 2010–2019. EO data at high resolution detect disturbances at lower or higher magnitude to forest C losses reported in NGHGI. Depending on resolution of the satellite product and disturbance detection approach, C losses from small-scale disturbances and management may be better detected, as higher spatial resolution allows capturing small scale heterogeneity. Despite overall agreement of different data streams, we find discrepancies of 2–3 fold difference in AGC and carbon losses estimated for each country between NGHGIs and EO-based datasets. We highlight regional differences across the continent and discuss advantages and challenges of the complementary data streams, with a focus on how high resolution EO and NGHGIs can benefit each other.
